critique: The single-page scene unmistakably shows a wood floor, wet mop, bucket, and spill, with convincing plank texture and a warm cinematic palette. The mop head and liquid are readable, but the huge spill dominates as a smooth gray mass with limited translucency or floor interaction, and the bucket is small and detached near the edge. The sparse title and tiny lower caption feel like editorial overlays rather than part of the scene. The trade-off is to keep the elegant minimal composition while adding enough material detail and narrative relationship to make the liquid and cleaning action believable rather than diagrammatic.
suggestion: Preserve the diagonal plank composition and restrained warm lighting. Refine the spill with semi-transparent layered edges, reflected plank lines, small satellite droplets, and localized highlights/shadows so it reads as water on wood rather than opaque gray paint. Bring the bucket slightly inward and connect it visually to the mop through a subtle wet trail; clarify the mop handle-to-head joint and add a few damp strands with varied curvature. Consolidate the title and small instruction into one quiet upper-left caption block, remove the nearly illegible corner copy, and keep all new detail subordinate to the mop-and-spill focal relationship.
